I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for an H2 uptake amount measured from the gas phase by a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow method (wt%, mmol/g, cm3/g, isotherm). None found. The only H2 sorption test (SI Fig. S16) puts NG in aqueous suspension, plots residual headspace H2 concentration (uM) by reduction gas detector against a blank, and reports no uptake value ('no significant differences'). Other H2 data are H2 formed by nZVI corrosion (Fig. 6).

I5.quote: Vinyl chloride (VC) is a dominant carcinogenic residual in many aged chlorinated solvent plumes, and it remains a huge challenge to clean it up.

notes: Water-remediation paper (VC reduction by nZVI with N-doped graphene). Closest candidate for I1: 'The sorption of NG materials towards H2 was also tested, but no significant differences were observed between different NGs (Fig. S16)' (main, p. 8, Section 3.4) and 'Hydrogen adsorption extent of NG materials produced at varying PT. Experimental conditions: 2 mL of pure H2 gas were added to sealed 10 ml vials containing 5 ml of 4 g/L of NG' (si1, p. 21, Fig. S16). The figure's y-axis is 'Hydrogen concentration (uM)' in the headspace for Blank and NG400-NG1100, with NG bars equal to or above the blank within error bars; no amount taken up per gram is given, the sorbent is dispersed in water rather than exposed to gas, and the method is batch headspace analysis, not gravimetric, volumetric or flow. No temperature or pressure is stated numerically for this test, so even if it were counted under I1, I3 would fail and the code would still be no_conditions_stated. Code is not 'electrochemical': no electrochemical charging is performed; the H*/H2 in Fig. 6 comes from nZVI anaerobic corrosion and is H2 formation, not uptake. For reference only (not assessed): supplier SSA 'graphene nanoplatelets (900394, specific surface area of 300 m2/g' (si1, p. 2, Text S1) and BET SSA of NG materials (main, p. 3, Section 2.5; si1, Fig. S5). Not a review; record.json is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF; no duplicate-data statement.
